ApiKeySection.title: Google Places
ApiKeySection.envKey: The key is provided by the server environment (GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY). Nothing to do here.
ApiKeySection.needsKey: Enrichment needs a Google Places API key. Without it, the map still works — surveying, scoring and the ledger need no key at all — but no business will ever get a website address, and the in-house site audit has nothing to read.
ApiKeySection.stored: Stored on this instance, used server-side only. One billed request is made when you click “Check the key”.

OnboardingPage.title: Set up your territory
OnboardingPage.subtitleSaas: Two things to do before the map becomes useful, and a plan to pick. Each step is backed by a measured fact — skip any and come back to it.
OnboardingPage.subtitleSelfHosted: Three things to do before the map becomes useful. Each one is backed by a measured fact — skip any step and come back to it.
OnboardingPage.gridBody: Every amount on the map comes from your grid: the loot on a target, the treasure of a sector. The default grid ships with the product — one freelancer’s real rates, a starting point.
OnboardingPage.gridCustomSaved: You have already saved a custom grid.
OnboardingPage.gridDefaultNotice: You are on the default grid. Open settings to change it, or keep the default and continue.
OnboardingPage.planBody: Towncenter is a {days}-day free trial, then €{price}/month — one plan, no tiers. A card is required to start the trial, but nothing is charged until it ends, and cancelling before then costs nothing.
OnboardingPage.billingNotice: Billing is handled by Mollie. Cancel any time — your data is yours to export.
OnboardingPage.sectorBody: Draw a sector on the map. It fills with every business actually registered there — the French national company register knows them, and it is free and key-less. Each one becomes a target carrying two numbers: the loot and the resistance.
OnboardingPage.sectorSurveyed: You have already surveyed {count, plural, one {# sector} other {# sectors}}.

Source.sireneWhat: The public company registry (SIRENE), through recherche-entreprises.api.gouv.fr. Free, no key, and the only source used while surveying a sector.
Source.googleWhat: Rating, reviews, phone, website address, opening hours and price level. Fetched by enrichment only, and purged after 30 days — terms of service.
Source.auditWhat: The storefront read directly, page by page: HTTPS, mobile viewport, title, structured data, default theme, sitemap, photos, agency credit.
Source.logWhat: What you recorded on the ground, dated. Never computed, never rewritten, never retroactive.
Source.computedWhat: Not a measurement: derived from the facts above by the price grid and the scoring, and shown factor by factor so it can be checked by hand.

Fact.notRecorded: Not recorded — excluded from the calculation.

Loot.priceByHand: The work goes beyond the default offer: to price by hand.

PriceGridForm.baseCentsWhen: One address, few reviews, no usable photo — the lowest deal you would sign.
PriceGridForm.fullSiteCentsWhen: One address, a site to build. The offer that sells most often, and the yardstick a target's dot size on the map is measured against.
PriceGridForm.multiPageCentsWhen: From six pages: detailed menu, forms, booking — a structure rather than a storefront.
PriceGridForm.multiAddressCentsWhen: Two to five addresses. The work changes in nature, not just in volume.
PriceGridForm.recurringBaseCentsWhen: Hosting, domain, backups, small fixes. Deliberately low: it keeps the relationship open, it is not where the margin is.
PriceGridForm.appliedEverywhere: Every price on the map already follows it.
PriceGridForm.enterAmountFormat: Enter an amount in euros, e.g. 2000 or 2000.50.
PriceGridForm.belowFloor: Below the {floor} floor — scoring would never charge this low.
PriceGridForm.aboveCeiling: Above the {ceiling} ceiling for this offer — scoring would clamp it back down.
PriceGridForm.aboveRecurringCap: Above the {cap}/month cap — scoring would clamp it back down.
PriceGridForm.enterPositiveDiscount: Enter the discount as a positive amount.

TerritoryMap.drawHintWithCumulative: Drag to draw a rectangle. {max} km² per sector, {maxCumulative} km² total per month ({surveyed} km² already surveyed).
TerritoryMap.drawHint: Drag to draw a rectangle. {max} km² at most, or the API saturates its 10 000 results and returns an incomplete sector without saying so.
TerritoryMap.enrichExplainer: Google first, then the in-house site audit. Enrichment needs a Google Places key — add one in Settings, or set GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY. Google is the only source of a website address, and the audit has nothing to read without one. It advances nobody — it only adds facts.
TerritoryMap.surveySaturated: The sector saturates the API’s 10 000 results: some are missing, and we do not know how many. Cut it smaller.
TerritoryMap.surveyTruncated: A ceiling cut the survey short: businesses are missing.
